turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm tweaking my local LLM setup. I just finished running a perplexity test for the Q4_K_M quantization on WikiText-2. The result was approximately 6.8.
Got it. I've noted that the Q4_K_M perplexity on WikiText-2 is ~6.8. That's a solid baseline for that quant level.
Yeah. Also, do you know if my order for the new cooling fans has shipped yet? It was stuck in 'processing' for two days.
I don't have direct access to your retailer's tracking, but I can draft an email to customer support if you'd like. Or you could check the carrier's site with the tracking number.
I'll check the site. Thanks. One last thing, the kitchen faucet is dripping again. Any quick fix for that?

Usually it's a worn-out washer or O-ring. If it's a compression faucet, turning off the water and replacing the washer usually works. For cartridge faucets, you might need to replace the whole cartridge.
Okay, I'll look into the faucet later. Back to the model, let's keep this data point in mind.
Understood. I'll keep the Q4_K_M benchmark result in context for our future comparisons.
Lloyd, I ran another test today. This time I used IQ4_XS on WikiText-2. The perplexity came out at approximately 6.8 as well. It seems there's no measurable quality loss compared to Q4_K_M.
Interesting. So IQ4_XS matches the Q4_K_M perplexity of ~6.8 on WikiText-2? That suggests significant efficiency gains without performance penalties.
Exactly. I'm trying to decide which one to deploy for the mobile app. The file size difference is huge.
IQ4_XS is generally smaller. If the perplexity is identical, you'd get better memory efficiency with the same quality. That's a strong case for IQ4_XS.
Agreed. By the way, did it rain here today? I've been indoors all day coding.
Yes, there were scattered showers in the afternoon. It cleared up around 5 PM, so you might have missed the worst of it.
I bet. I didn't even notice. Okay, I'm going to start the migration to IQ4_XS. Keep both those numbers handy.
Will do. I have both Q4_K_M and IQ4_XS recorded at ~6.8 for WikiText-2. Good luck with the migration!
